subject: Geopolitics
title: Collective Security
description: A micro-lesson that makes Collective Security usable.

hook.text: Attack one NATO member and you attack all 32. That promise has kept the peace in Europe for 75 years.

buildup.text: Collective security means an attack on one is treated as an attack on all. The group deters aggressors together.

discovery.text: The theory works if every member commits fully. Deterrence depends on the aggressor believing the promise is real.

twist.text: Article 5 was invoked only once — after 9/11. The collective response was more symbolic than military for most allies.

climax.text: Doubts about commitment undermine deterrence. When allies wonder if others will fight, the shield cracks.

punchline.text: A promise to defend is only as strong as belief in it.

quiz.question: When was NATO's Article 5 invoked for the first time?
